newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures end sharply lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures end sharply lower.

text.p: U.S. debt futures ended the first trading day of the year sharply lower, and most traders and analysts are looking for further declines on mounting evidence that the U.S. economic growth rate is not slowing.

"Today was a complete shellacking," one T-bond analyst said about the strong selloff in both the bond and Eurodollar pits. "The only thing one can say is that investors are nervous that growth will bring higher inflation."
December National Association of Purchasing Management (NAPM) index rose to 54.0, shocking dealers and traders who were pricing in a decline to 51.5, from 52.7 in November.
The price component in the NAPM index also rose to 51.5 versus 45.9 in November, adding to evidence that the rate of growth in the U.S. economy was not slowing.
March T-bonds lost more than a point immediately after the data were released, with the contract breezing through the intraday low of 112-18/32 on heavy sell-stop orders at 112-22/32 to 112-24/32.
The market continued to attract liquidation, as traders were still smarting from Tuesday's sharp sell-off.
"Tuesday caught a lot of people off-guard," a trader said.
Some traders, who turned short on Tuesday, covered those positions at the start of Thursday's session.
The increase in the U.S. weekly jobless claims encouraged shortcovering in Treasury bond and note futures contracts. A French firm alone bought 9,000 five-year notes and 2,500 10-year notes.
But the shortcovering rally proved disappointing because March was unable to rise to 113-02/32.
"We traded poorly on good news," a trader added.
In addition, analysts said most technical indicators before the opening were bearish.

March T-bonds fell to 111-05/32, retracing about 50 percent of the contract's rise from September to December. Traders said March is bound to test the actual retracement level of 111-00 in the near term.
March broke through 111-13/32, the upper end of a seven-month range to levels last seen in late October.
June Eurodollars fell through the Dec 6 low of 94.22 immediately after the NAPM data, while March Eurodollars tested the month low of 94.36.
On Friday, U.S. November construction spending data will be released at 1000 EST/1500 GMT.

At the end of pit trade, March T-bonds were off 1-08/32 at 111-12/32, March 10-year notes were 22/32 lower at 108-14/32, March Eurodollars were six basis points lower at 94.38, June Eurodollars were down nine bps at 94.19 and June T-bills were also down nine bps at 94.74.
